title: Load-controlled Hertz contact: contact radius and indentation vs closed form (case pool FEM-HERTZ-CONTACT)

gates.quantity: |a_FE/a_Hertz - 1|, a/R = 0.05, h/a = 0.0075 (primary linear-zero-crossing estimator)
gates.reference: a = (3 P R / (4 E*))^(1/3), E* = E/(1-nu^2) (rigid indenter)

gates.quantity: |delta_FE/delta_Hertz - 1|, a/R = 0.05, h/a = 0.0075
gates.reference: delta = a^2 / R

gates.quantity: |indentation error(h/a=0.0075) - indentation error(h/a=0.03)| (pct points)
gates.reference: the indentation error saturates at a mesh-independent plateau; refinement must not move it by more than 0.5 pp
gates.note: a stricter 'monotone decrease' gate was drafted first and FAILED by 1.4e-3 pp: the error plateaus at -1.01% instead of tending to zero, i.e. the residual is a systematic model offset, not discretisation noise

gates.quantity: |a_FE/a_Hertz - 1|, a/R = 0.1, h/a = 0.0075 (primary linear-zero-crossing estimator)
gates.reference: a = (3 P R / (4 E*))^(1/3), E* = E/(1-nu^2) (rigid indenter)

gates.quantity: |delta_FE/delta_Hertz - 1|, a/R = 0.1, h/a = 0.0075
gates.reference: delta = a^2 / R

gates.quantity: |indentation error(h/a=0.0075) - indentation error(h/a=0.03)| (pct points)
gates.reference: the indentation error saturates at a mesh-independent plateau; refinement must not move it by more than 0.5 pp
gates.note: a stricter 'monotone decrease' gate was drafted first and FAILED by 1.4e-3 pp: the error plateaus at -1.01% instead of tending to zero, i.e. the residual is a systematic model offset, not discretisation noise

gates.quantity: |p0_FE/p0_Hertz - 1| from the mass-matrix consistent pressure field
max penetration / prescribed indentation (constraint violation)
gates.reference: ALM fixed point: penetration -> 0
gates.note: ALM tolerance is 1e-10 relative to the displacement scale

gates.quantity: |sum(lambda) / P - 1| (load-control equilibrium)
gates.reference: prescribed P

gates.quantity: || (K u)_free + lambda || / ||lambda|| (free-dof force balance)
gates.reference: discrete equilibrium of the assembled system
gates.note: regression guard: the pre-m166xx sign convention reported exactly 2.0 here, so this gate could never pass and a real imbalance would have been invisible

gates.quantity: spread of contact_radius over rho*E/a in {0.3, 1, 3} (% of mean)
gates.reference: the ALM parameter must not change the converged state

gates.quantity: spread of indentation over rho*E/a in {0.3, 1, 3} (% of mean)
gates.reference: the ALM parameter must not change the converged state

gates.quantity: change in indentation error between domain depth 48a and 96a (pct points)
gates.reference: finite-patch truncation must be resolved by the accepted depth 96a

gates.quantity: change in contact_radius_linear error between domain depth 48a and 96a (pct points)
gates.reference: finite-patch truncation must be resolved by the accepted depth 96a

gates.quantity: |e_inf(delta)|: Richardson limit of the indentation error as depth/ a -> inf (a/R = 0.05, h/a = 0.015)
gates.reference: delta = a^2/R (Hertz 1882; Johnson 1985 §4.2) at infinite half-space

gates.quantity: |e_inf(delta)| against the pre-declared 0.5% bound that separates 'unconverged truncation' from 'model bias'
gates.reference: H_trunc accepted iff the extrapolated residual is <= 0.5%
gates.note: a FAIL here is a *result*, not an error: it quantifies the irreducible model bias of the Q4 paraboloid model (see verdict in truncation_extrapolation.json)

gates.quantity: number of levels where the indentation error does NOT decay in magnitude towards the infinite-domain limit
gates.reference: a truncation error must vanish as the boundary recedes

gates.quantity: |observed decay order of the indentation-error sequence| (depth doubling)
gates.reference: admissible band [0.5, 3]; an order far below the band means the ladder is still in the pre-asymptotic regime

gates.quantity: spread (pp) of |contact-radius error| over the depth ladder 96a -> 768a
gates.reference: the contact radius is a near-field measure: if the depth ladder moves it, the reported a is contaminated by truncation

gates.quantity: |e_inf(delta)| at the second load (a/R = 0.10, h/a = 0.015)
gates.reference: delta = a^2/R at infinite half-space; load independence of the plateau is what made it look mesh-independent

gates.quantity: |e_delta(dz=a/6) - e_delta(dz=a/24)| (pct points), radial near field bit-identical
gates.reference: a genuinely mesh-independent model bias would leave e_delta unchanged (0 pp); a discretisation artefact of the unrefined vertical spacing must move it
gates.note: the h/a ladder refined r only and never dz, so 'mesh independent' was a one-directional statement; this gate makes the dz axis part of the record

gates.quantity: shift (pp) of |e_delta| when the stretched far field is refined from 16 to 64 vertical (26 -> 104 radial) layers
gates.reference: H_far predicted a collapse of the offset; the pre-declared equivalence band is 0.05 pp
gates.note: passing this gate means 'the far field is NOT the mechanism', i.e. H_far is rejected; the extrapolated limit only moves -0.4278 -> -0.3878 %

gates.quantity: |e_delta| at dz=a/48, depth 768a (case-pool metric, vertical-refined near field)
gates.reference: delta = a^2/R (Hertz 1882; Johnson 1985 4.2), case-pool band 3%

gates.quantity: |p0_FE/p0_Hertz - 1| (mass-matrix consistent) at dz=a/24, depth 768a
gates.reference: p0 = 3P/(2 pi a^2); the 5% band of the case certificate does not apply to this refined model, 0.05% is the pre-declared study bound

gates.quantity: |(delta/P)_FE / (delta/P)_Hertz - 1|, a/R = 0.05, h/a = 0.0075
gates.reference: Hertz compliance: delta/P = (9/(16 R E*^2))^(1/3) P^(-1/3)
gates.note: probe: post-hoc grade of the compliance metric from result.json

gates.quantity: |(delta/P)_FE / (delta/P)_Hertz - 1|, a/R = 0.10, h/a = 0.0075
gates.reference: Hertz compliance: delta/P = (9/(16 R E*^2))^(1/3) P^(-1/3)
gates.note: probe: post-hoc grade of the compliance metric from result.json

gates.quantity: spread of {a_linear, a_fit, a_fit_consistent} as % of mean, a/R = 0.05, h/a = 0.0075
gates.reference: all three contact-radius estimators must agree on the finest mesh

gates.quantity: spread of {a_linear, a_fit, a_fit_consistent} as % of mean, a/R = 0.10, h/a = 0.0075
gates.reference: all three contact-radius estimators must agree on the finest mesh

limitations: Rigid parabolic indenter on an elastic half-space: the FE model is the Hertz reduction itself, so this grades the discretisation and the contact algorithm, not a deformable-body generalisation.

The contact radius is estimated from the computed pressure field (linear zero crossing between the last two active nodes); at a/R = 0.02 the patch edge falls between coarse nodes and the estimator degrades -- recorded as probe_low_load, deliberately outside the gates.
Depth truncation is a modelling error, not a discretisation error: it is quantified by the truncation ladder rather than eliminated.
No friction; no material or geometric nonlinearity (linear elasticity, small strain).
The consistent-pressure contact-radius estimator is noisy on coarse meshes (h/a >= 0.015); the spread gate only applies to the finest mesh (h/a = 0.0075).
